why_angle: Tech Advisor and iTechGuides gave no measured runtimes. iTechGuides repeats only Samsung's own rating, and neither covers the Lenovo Yoga Tab. This page lines up Notebookcheck's Wi-Fi browsing runtimes from one lab for all four 11-inch candidates. They show the overall pick, the Galaxy Tab S11, lasts the shortest (11.2 h against 17.7 h for the Yoga Tab). Angle A scored higher on standout but can't be completed, because the update promise for the S10 FE and A11+ has no clear maker source.

page.title: Best 11-inch Android Tablet (2026): Galaxy Tab S11, with Measured Battery Life
page.desc: The Galaxy Tab S11 is the best 11-inch Android tablet for its screen and S Pen, but Notebookcheck measured 11.2 h of browsing against 17.7 h for the Lenovo Yoga Tab.
page.answer: Short answer. The best 11-inch Android tablet in 2026 is the Samsung Galaxy Tab S11: an OLED screen, the S Pen in the box and 7 years of security updates. Its weak spot is battery life: Notebookcheck measured 11.2 h of Wi-Fi browsing, against 17.7 h for the Lenovo Yoga Tab.

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • Yoga Tab vs Tab S11, battery: 17.7 h ÷ 11.2 h = 1.58, so the Yoga Tab browses about 58% longer, or 6.5 h more per charge.
  • Tab S10 FE vs Tab S11: 14.8 h − 11.2 h = 3.6 h more browsing from the cheaper Samsung. Samsung's US store listed the S10 FE at $549.99 and the Tab S11 128 GB at $999.99 on 2026-11-11, a gap of $999.99 − $549.99 = $450.
  • Tab A11+ vs Tab S11: 14.9 h − 11.2 h = 3.7 h more, from a smaller 7,040 mAh battery. At Samsung US prices that day, $999.99 − $299.99 = $700 less.
  • Screen: Notebookcheck measured a 1,575 cd/m² peak on the Tab S11, against 743 cd/m² on the Yoga Tab and 543 cd/m² on the A11+. 1,575 ÷ 743 = 2.1 times as bright at peak.
  • Sustained speed: in Notebookcheck's 3DMark Wild Life Extreme stress test, the Yoga Tab held 82.1% of its first-run score and the Tab S11 held 66.7%. 82.1 − 66.7 = 15.4 points less throttling on the Yoga.

Battery life measured in one lab

All four runtimes come from Notebookcheck's Wi-Fi browsing test, which loads web pages in a loop until the battery runs out. For the Tab S11, S10 FE and Yoga Tab, Notebookcheck sets the screen to 150 cd/m². Because the method is the same, the hours can be compared directly, unlike the makers' 'up to' video ratings.

Battery size doesn't explain the gap. The Yoga Tab's 8,860 mAh cell is only 8,860 ÷ 8,400 = 1.05, or about 5%, larger than the Tab S11's, yet it lasts 58% longer. The A11+ has 16% less capacity than the S11 (7,040 vs 8,400 mAh) and still lasts 3.7 h longer. In this test the S11's Dimensity 9400+ and 120 Hz OLED panel draw more power than the other three.

So the Tab S11 earns its place on the screen and the pen, not on endurance. {buy:samsung-galaxy-tab-s11-128gb-wifi} The S Pen in its box has no Bluetooth, so it can't act as a camera remote or use Air Actions, and Samsung says buying an S Pen Pro doesn't add them on this tablet. Notebookcheck also measured 480 Hz PWM flicker on the S11's panel and found none on the Yoga Tab or the A11+. If you're sensitive to flicker, that matters. Samsung promises up to 7 Android upgrades and 7 years of security updates, counted from global launch rather than from your purchase date.

If you want a Samsung with the pen included and longer battery life for less money, the Tab S10 FE ran 14.8 h in the same test. It has a 90 Hz LCD instead of OLED. {buy:samsung-galaxy-tab-s10-fe-128gb-wifi}

Before buying a Yoga Tab, check which generation it is. The tested 2025 model (Snapdragon 8 Gen 3) gets 3 Android upgrades, ending at Android 18, and 4 years of security patches, per MyNextTablet and Android Headlines. It also has no microSD slot. The Yoga Tab Gen 2 launched in September 2026. It has the same 11.1-inch size, an 11,000 mAh battery, Android upgrades through Android 24 and security updates through 2033, at a $729.99 launch price (9to5Google). Notebookcheck hasn't published a battery test for it yet.
